newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Arthuis hits at Socialists' programme.
newsitem.headline: France's Arthuis hits at Socialists' programme.

text.p: France's Finance Minister Jean Arthuis criticised on Saturday the opposition Socialist party for failing to detail the cost of its economic programme.
"I do not believe in a policy that promises everything without saying how much it will exactly cost," Arthuis said in an interview with Radio Classique.

Arthuis, a member of the ruling UDF-RPR center-right coalition, also said that the Socialists' programme, which calls for a cut in the work week and plans to create 700,000 jobs for the young, would require raising public spending and thus limit growth.
Arthuis also criticised the Socialists' opposition to the privatisation of France Telecom, saying this would penalise the company in an increasingly competitive environment.
He also said that the state needed the 30 to 50 billion francs that will be generated by the sale to recapitalise other groups.

On Friday, the Socialists said in their manifesto ahead of parliamentary elections on May 25-June 1 that they planned to promote jobs without raising public spending. They proposed a government backed-scheme to create 700,000 jobs, including 350,000 public sector jobs and to cut the work week to 35 hours from 39 wihout loss of salary.
They also vowed to protect public services in security, education, transport, health, post and telecoms.

Arthuis also told Radio Classique that a reduction in charges burdening the low-wages sector must be a priority for the ruling centre-right coalition, if it wins the May 25-June 1 parliamentary elections.
Arthuis did not say which charges he was referring to.
He also said that the cuts could be progressively extended to other wages sectors as soon as the state of public finances and economic growth allows.
"Due to our budgetary means we must target the most modest wages and particularly the manufacturing sector," Arthuis said in an interview with Radio Classique.
"We must progressively extend the measures to the whole wages sector," he added.
Arthuis said that low-paid workers in the manufacturing sector were the most vulnerable to possible industry transfers, citing the crisis in the textile sector.
The state has already set up an aid plan for the textile sector that involves cuts and other exemptions in social security contributions for low-paid workers.
